RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-D304BE9399-97960
Member: Riley Lawson
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Date of notice: 2026-08-24

To the Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), communicated in the notice referenced above. The stated reason for denial is that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed, for the reasons set out below, supported by my treating surgeon, Dr. Duval, and the enclosed records.

Note on quoted material: The only text below placed in quotation marks is text I obtained directly from the Cigna/eviCore coverage guideline "Hip Surgery-Arthroscopic and Open Procedures" (CMM-314), the version effective July 1, 2025, which is the document eviCore/Cigna has published as governing medical-necessity review of arthroscopic hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI), including CPT 29914. I was not able to independently re-verify that the identical wording appears in the version of this guideline dated August 4, 2026 (the version that may have been in effect on the date of my denial notice), because the copy of that later version I was able to obtain was truncated before reaching the FAI-specific criteria section. I ask Cigna to confirm in writing which exact version and section of CMM-314 (or any other coverage policy) was applied to my request, and to apply the criteria below if they are unchanged, or to identify any differences if they are not.

1. Imaging criteria

The guideline states that FAI surgery is medically necessary when imaging shows, among other things:

"Femoroacetabular impingement confirmed on X-ray, MRI, or CT with ANY of the following findings: Alpha angle greater than 50 degrees; Pistol-grip deformity; Decrease of femoral head-neck offset; Acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign); Coxa profunda — Presence of Tönnis Grade 0-1 osteoarthritis."

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-07-23 documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees — well above the 50-degree threshold — with joint space preserved and Tönnis grade 0. This satisfies both the alpha-angle finding and the Tönnis 0–1 requirement stated in the guideline.

2. Physical exam and symptom criteria

The guideline further requires:

"Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: Positive Anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation); Limited passive hip internal rotation... Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and that significantly limits activities."

My exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. Functionally, I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting and I am unable to run or squat — activities that involve hip flexion, directly matching the symptom pattern the guideline describes as flexion-provoked, activity-limiting groin pain.

3. Conservative-treatment criteria — the basis for this appeal

The denial states that an adequate trial of conservative treatment was not documented. The guideline requires:

"Failure of provider-directed non-surgical treatment for at least three (3) months duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated): An image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within 2 weeks after the injection)."

The record documents far more than three months of provider-directed non-surgical treatment:

- 18 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest;
- 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification (2026-03-28 to 2026-07-04, 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note);
- 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-26 that produced approximately two weeks of partial relief.

This corticosteroid injection response — partial pain reduction lasting about two weeks — meets the guideline's stated standard of "any degree of pain reduction achieved within 2 weeks after the injection." [The submitted records provided to me do not specify whether this injection was administered under image guidance; Dr. Duval's office will supply confirmation of imaging guidance, or an addendum note, if that detail is missing from the file Cigna reviewed.] Taken together, more than three months — in fact 14 weeks of formal physical therapy alone, on top of 6 months of medication management and an injection trial — of documented, provider-directed conservative care preceded the request for surgery, satisfying the duration and modality requirements quoted above.

4. Absence of contraindications to surgery

The record also reflects no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, none of which raise any contraindication to the requested arthroscopic procedure.

Conclusion

Based on the criteria in the guideline as quoted above and the enclosed clinical documentation — the physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-28 to 2026-07-04, 16 visits), medication and injection records, the 2026-07-23 MRI arthrogram report, and Dr. Duval's clinic notes and exam findings — I believe the record satisfies the imaging, physical-exam, symptom, and conservative-treatment elements of the applicable medical-necessity guideline. I ask that Cigna reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29914.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-28–2026-07-04)
- Medication/injection records, including the 2026-04-26 corticosteroid injection note
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-07-23
- Office/exam notes from Dr. Duval documenting provocative testing and functional limitation
- [Any letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval]
- A copy of the denial notice (reference POC-D304BE9399-97960)

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the applicable review timeline. If this appeal is denied, please provide the specific policy version, section, and criteria relied upon, along with information on my right to an independent external review, as required under applicable law.

I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions.

Sincerely,

Riley Lawson
